For Respondents: Mr. R. Prathap Kuma Additional Public Prosecutor
judgment_text:
Petition filed under Article 226 of the Constitution of India, praying to issue a Writ of Habeas Corpus, directing the respondents to grant 3 months leave without escort to the petitioner's husband namely Mr. C. Raj Mohan, S/o Chandra Mohan, aged about 43 years (C.T. No. 6584) now confined in Central Prison, Salem for Kidney transplantation to the petitioner's son namely Master. Sanjay, aged about 16 years in pursuant to the medical records.

The Order of the Court was delivered by

M.M. Sundresh, J.:— The petitioner is the wife of the convict, who has been under incarceration for having committed offence punishable under Sections 302, 364, 341 IPC. Ordinary Leave has been sought for on the premise that the convict will have to make arrangements for surgery of kidney transplantation of his son Master. Sanjay, aged about 16 years.

2. The learned Additional Public Prosecutor submitted that the convict's son is suffering from kidney ailment viz., bilateral chronic medical rental disease.

3. We find that the convict will have to be given 30 days of ordinary leave inasmuch as the purpose for leave is not in dispute.

4. According, we direct the respondents to grant ordinary leave to the convict for 30 days subject to the usual conditions that can be imposed by the respondents. The convict shall be released from the prison at 10.00 a.m. on 20.09.2019 and that the convict shall return back to the prison at or before 05.00 p.m. on 21.10.2019. The convict shall be accompanied by adequate escorts and the expenses for providing escorts shall be borne by the State. We make it clear that the day on which the convict is released from the prison and the day on which he is re-admitted will have to be excluded from the leave.

5. In the result, the Habeas Corpus Petition is disposed of with the above directions.

6. List this matter on 22.09.2019 for reporting compliance.
